meta.title: Nitto Boseki — Tsutomu Yatsui's specialty glass fiber and electronic materials pivot from textile heritage
meta.abstract: Nitto Boseki Co., Ltd. (3110.T on Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime) is a Japanese specialty materials company originally founded in 1923 as a textile spinning company. Through multi-decade transformation, Nitto Boseki has become the principal Japanese supplier of specialty E-glass and low-dielectric (low-Dk) glass fiber for printed circuit board (PCB) substrates used in advanced AI server and high-frequency electronics applications. The strategic narrative through 2024-2026 has been the low-Dk glass fiber scaling driven by AI server PCB demand for high-frequency, low-loss substrate materials.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## A Specialty Niche Finds Its Moment

When spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure steepened through 2023-2026, Nitto Boseki Co., Ltd. found itself pulled from the margins of the Japanese materials sector into a supply-chain position it had spent decades preparing for. The company, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market as **3110**, kept its headquarters in Tokyo and its head office in Fukushima, and by the frozen date it described itself as a supplier of Special Glass used in printed wiring boards and semiconductor package substrates that supported the digital-society push embedded in its "global niche" strategy. [Company profile](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/corporate/about/index.htm), [Long-Term Vision](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/vision.htm), [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm)

## Heritage: From Spinning to Special Glass

Nittobo's corporate records traced the business to February 1898 (Koriyama Kenshi Boseki), April 1918 (Fukushima Seiren Seishi) and April 1923, when NITTO BOSEKI CO., LTD. was established. The centennial history page showed how a textile company became a glass-fiber company: industrial glass fiber and rock wool in 1938, glass wool in 1949, glass cloth for printed wiring boards in 1969, T-glass in 1984 and NE-glass in 1998. [Company profile](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/corporate/about/index.htm), [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

## Leadership and Governance

By the frozen date the chief executive was no longer Hiroyuki Tada but Hisanobu Hayashi. Nittobo's directors-and-officers page listed Hayashi as Representative and Chief Executive Officer as of 1 April 2026, while Tada - who had become Representative and Chief Executive Officer in April 2024 - had moved to Director and Deputy Chairman. The governance report still showed a seven-member board with four external directors, consistent with the group's company-with-nomination-committee structure. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html), [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

## Financial Profile: Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2026

The company's latest full-year disclosure inside the frozen window was the result released on 12 May 2026 for the fiscal year ended 31 March 2026. Nittobo reported net sales of ¥118.229 billion, operating profit of ¥20.819 billion, ordinary profit of ¥21.544 billion and profit attributable to owners of parent of ¥41.770 billion. The operating margin rose to 17.6 per cent from 15.1 per cent a year earlier, while ROE reached 27.5 per cent. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

Electronic Materials carried the profit story. In the statutory segment note, the business generated ¥49.265 billion of net sales and ¥19.391 billion of operating profit; in the investor presentation, where Electronic Materials included intersegment sales, the equivalent sales figure was ¥61.4 billion. Management attributed the outperformance to "strong demand related to AI servers" and to sales of low-thermal-expansion and low-dielectric Special Glass. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

The balance-sheet side of the same disclosure reinforced how quickly the company had changed shape. Total assets reached ¥283.038 billion, net assets ¥180.383 billion and cash and cash equivalents ¥61.835 billion, while the stock-information page put shares outstanding at 37,723,012 and the shareholder count at 18,579 as of 31 March 2026. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [Stock information](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/memo.htm)

The company-profile page also showed how substantial the enterprise had become even before any market multiple was applied: paid-in capital of ¥19.6 billion and 2,793 consolidated employees, of whom 867 were at the parent company, as of 31 March 2026. That was a reminder that the Special Glass story sat inside a mid-sized industrial group with real balance-sheet and personnel depth, not inside a single-product venture. [Company profile](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/corporate/about/index.htm)

## The Glass Fiber Inflection

The company's own materials framed the demand inflection in two product families rather than in one generic glass-cloth market. T-glass, which Nittobo described as high-elasticity and low-thermal-expansion glass, was used in semiconductor package substrates; NE-glass, developed in the 1990s, was described in the 2025 integrated report as the de facto standard for low-dielectric glass and was being adopted for motherboards of switches required for high-speed communication between chips in AI servers. The same report said demand had risen sharply as AI servers grew more powerful and as larger semiconductor packages created more severe warping and thermal-expansion problems. [T-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/t-glass.htm), [NE-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/ne-glass.htm), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

## Capacity Scaling

The dated primary record diverged sharply from several of the secondary figures circulating in late 2025. Nittobo's integrated report said that in August 2025 the company decided to expand glass fiber cloth production at the Fukushima Enterprise Center, with production scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of FY2026. Separately, the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry approved a supply-security plan on 7 August 2025 for low-thermal-expansion glass cloth for advanced logic ICs: the approval summary put the project in Fukushima City, targeted supply from July 2027, described the capacity increase as about 200 per cent, and stated required funding of about ¥72 billion with a maximum subsidy of about ¥24 billion. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [METI approval summary](https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/economy/economic_security/semicon/nintei_anpohandoutai_keikaku_27.pdf)

By 12 May 2026 management had also moved the financial plan forward. For the fiscal year ending 31 March 2027, Nittobo forecast net sales of ¥137.0 billion, operating profit of ¥26.0 billion, capital investment of ¥45.0 billion and R&D spending of ¥4.6 billion. At the same briefing, the company revised its FY2027 medium-term targets to ¥155.0 billion of net sales, ¥36.0 billion of operating profit, approximately ¥120 billion of four-year capital investment and approximately ¥16 billion of four-year R&D spend. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

## Competitive Positioning

Nittobo's own language was more measured than the popular single-source narrative of an unchallenged monopoly, but it was still unusually direct. In the 2025 integrated report, management said Chinese and Taiwanese companies were "aggressively catching up" in Special Glass while Nittobo still held an "overwhelming competitive advantage" in both quality and production capacity for low-thermal-expansion glass. The current medium-term plan showed the next step in that defence: next-generation Special Glass programmes labelled NEZ, V and DXII, and the technology roadmap in the integrated report also identified Vlex as the low-CTE, low-loss performance target beyond today's T-glass. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm)

The customer-facing follow-through was visible in Nittobo's own October 8, 2025 press release for TPCA Show Taipei 2025, where Nittobo Taiwan said it would exhibit next-generation Special Glass including low-CTE glass, low-DK glass and ultra-thin glass cloth. That did not amount to a customer list, but it did show the company actively commercialising the next wave of products into the Taiwan PCB ecosystem before the frozen date. [TPCA Show Taipei 2025 release](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/news/pdf/20251008_newsrelease.pdf)

chapters.title: From 1923 Nippon Spinning through specialty materials pivot to AI server PCB substrate
chapters.body:
## Origins in Silk and Spinning: Fukushima, 1898-1923

Nittobo's own company-profile page dated its roots to February 1898, when Koriyama Kenshi Boseki Co., Ltd. was established in Koriyama, and April 1918, when Fukushima Seiren Seishi Co., Ltd. was established in Fukushima. In April 1923 those lines came together as NITTO BOSEKI CO., LTD.; the centennial history page said Fukushima Boseki, formerly Fukushima Seiren Seishi, integrated with Katakura Seishi Iwashiro Bosekisho, formerly Koriyama Kenshi Boseki, and took the Nitto Boseki name. [Company profile](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/corporate/about/index.htm), [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

The Great Kanto Earthquake struck later that same year, but the company's own historical narrative placed the decisive event for Nittobo not in Tokyo's destruction but in the April 1923 corporate integration that created the present entity. The name "Nitto," the company said, invoked Japan and the founders' wish to be renewed each day as a spinning operator in the east. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

---

## A Discovery on the Margins: Glass Fiber Before the War

On the centennial history page, Nittobo said it succeeded in the industrial production of glass fiber in 1938 and in rock wool the same year, the latter a first in Japan. After the war, the same record showed the Koriyama factory starting glass wool production by the spraying method in 1949, also described as a domestic first. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

That chronology mattered because it showed that the company's move into glass was not a 2020s improvisation. By the time AI infrastructure spending became the market's obsession, Nittobo had already spent almost nine decades in glass-fiber production and more than five decades in electronic materials.

---

## Electronics as the New Loom: The 1969 Inflection

The centennial history page dated the electronic-materials pivot to 1969, when Nittobo launched glass cloth for printed wiring boards to serve the advance of computers and integrated circuits. Public company materials later described that business as the ancestor of the current Electronic Materials Business Division. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html), [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm)

The medical line was also older than the current AI narrative sometimes implied. Nittobo's history page dated the start of blood-coagulation in-vitro diagnostic reagent production to 1982, while the group later built NITTOBO MEDICAL in 1987. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

The intervening chronology also showed how broad the company's reinvention had been. The same official history recorded proprietary staple-fiber industrial production in 1933, the launch of the Nittobo Dishcloth in 1960, invention of specialty chemical PAS in 1963, and the 1986 acquisition of International Immunology Corporation, the predecessor of Nittobo America. These were not peripheral curiosities: they explained why a company that began in spinning later possessed a chemicals franchise, a diagnostics franchise and a U.S. biological-raw-material operation alongside glass fiber. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

---

## T-Glass, Taiwan and the Route into Asian Electronics

The company recorded 1984 as the year it launched T-glass, a high-strength, low-thermal-expansion Special Glass that was first used in advanced composites and later in semiconductor package substrates for high-speed processing and highly reliable servers and smartphones. Four years later, in 1988, it established Nittobo Norplex Oak Co., Ltd. in Taiwan as a joint-venture producer of glass fiber yarn, the predecessor of NITTOBO ASIA Glass Fiber Co., Ltd. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html), [T-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/t-glass.htm)

The Taiwan position deepened over time. Nittobo's history page showed Baotek Industrial Materials Ltd. in Taiwan becoming a consolidated subsidiary in 2019 and a new Special Glass factory being established at NITTOBO ASIA Glass Fiber Co., Ltd. in 2021, creating what the company called an all-in-one output system from Special Glass yarn to cloth on Taiwan's main island. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

The historical record also extended into the medical and overseas lanes. In 2015 the company received the Japanese agriculture ministry's prize for development of an in-vitro diagnostic reagent using genetically modified silkworms, while in 2022 Nittobo America expanded its California base. The point was less that each milestone altered the investment case on its own than that the group had kept building adjacent capabilities even while Special Glass became the flagship. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

The 2000s history rounded out the picture of a company that kept retooling rather than merely defending old product lines. The centennial page recorded the 2006 launch of Flat Fiber for molded products such as smartphone cases and automobile parts, the 2018 launch of an IgG4 measuring reagent kit for automated analyzers, and the 2019 acquisitions of Kamiya Biomedical and Capricorn Products in the United States. By the time AI-server demand made Special Glass famous, the group had already proved willing to reshape adjacent businesses through both internal development and bolt-on transactions. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

---

## The Low-Dielectric Bet: NE-Glass and the Frequency Frontier

Nittobo dated the launch of NE-glass to 1998. On the current product page, the company described NE-glass as an independently developed technology with lower alkaline-earth content and higher boric-acid content than general-purpose E-glass, giving it a dielectric constant of 4.8 at 1 GHz against 6.8 for E-glass and a dielectric dissipation factor of 0.0015 against 0.0035 for E-glass. [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html), [NE-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/ne-glass.htm)

That product decision became strategically consequential much later. The integrated report published in late 2025 said NE-glass had become the de facto standard for low-dielectric glass and was being adopted for the motherboards of switches used for high-speed chip-to-chip communication in AI servers. The same report said the company had begun rolling out NER-glass as communication speeds rose further. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm)

---

## The AI Inflection: From Long Gestation to Visible Scarcity

By the time the fiscal year ended 31 March 2026, the financial results finally matched the technical narrative. Nittobo reported that strong demand related to AI servers and robust sales of low-thermal-expansion and low-dielectric Special Glass drove Electronic Materials revenue to ¥49.265 billion and operating profit to ¥19.391 billion. In the investor presentation accompanying those results, management said the market demand visible by then was roughly two to three times what it had assumed when the FY2024-2027 plan was formulated. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

The same primary sources also made clear that this was not a single-product boom. T-glass adoption had risen as larger semiconductor packages created warping problems; NE-glass and its successors had ridden the push to faster communications equipment and AI-server motherboards; and the company's 2025-2026 disclosures pointed to further investment in Japan and overseas rather than a one-quarter opportunistic response. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm)

chapters.title: Glass fiber, textiles, food and pharma, environmental and engineering
chapters.body:
## A Reporting Structure That No Longer Matched the Old Four-Bucket Story

By the frozen date, Nittobo's own reporting had already outgrown the older shorthand of "glass fiber, textiles, food and pharma, environmental and engineering." The FY2024-2027 medium-term plan said the group had reorganized from three divisions to five business divisions on 1 April 2024, and the full-year results released on 12 May 2026 disclosed performance for Electronic Materials, Medical, Composite Materials, Materials Solution and Insulation Materials, plus Other Businesses. The shift mattered because it showed where textiles now sat in the portfolio: inside Materials Solution rather than as a standalone strategic axis. [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

| FY ended 31 March 2026 | Net sales | Operating profit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Electronic Materials | ¥49.265bn | ¥19.391bn |
| Medical | ¥13.850bn | ¥2.431bn |
| Composite Materials | ¥13.401bn | -¥0.122bn |
| Materials Solution | ¥9.515bn | ¥0.588bn |
| Insulation Materials | ¥15.136bn | ¥0.202bn |
| Other Businesses | ¥17.059bn | ¥0.488bn |

## Electronic Materials: The Strategic Core

This was the division the market cared about, and the filings justified that attention. Nittobo's Electronic Materials page said the business provided Special Glass for printed wiring-board materials supporting 5G, 6G, high-speed communications and semiconductor innovation. The FY2026 results report then showed how thoroughly that strategy was dominating group profitability: Electronic Materials generated 41.7 per cent of consolidated sales but almost all of group operating profit. In the briefing presentation, the company also showed Electronic Materials sales at ¥61.4 billion when intersegment sales were included, again underlining the division's strategic weight. [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

Nittobo's own product disclosures made clear that "Electronic Materials" was not a generic FR-4 exposure. T-glass was positioned as a high-elasticity, low-thermal-expansion material for semiconductor package substrates, while NE-glass and NER-glass were positioned around low dielectric constant and low dissipation factor for the higher-speed communications stack. [T-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/t-glass.htm), [NE-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/ne-glass.htm), [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm)

## Medical: A Mature Second Pillar

The Medical Business remained a real business rather than a historical afterthought. The company described it as an integrated chain from raw materials to finished in-vitro diagnostic reagents, with a strong domestic position in immunoturbidimetry reagents and global deployment of its products. In the year ended 31 March 2026 it produced ¥13.850 billion of sales and ¥2.431 billion of operating profit. [Medical Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/medical/index.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

That mattered strategically because it explained why management kept speaking of Special Glass and medical as the first two pillars of growth in the medium-term plan. Even at the height of the AI-server narrative, the medical franchise remained the group's clearest non-cyclical earnings counterweight. [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

## Composite Materials: Industrial Breadth Without the AI Premium

The Composite Materials Business supplied glass fiber as plastic reinforcing material for uses ranging from automotive parts to smartphone casings and bathtubs. The company reported ¥13.401 billion of sales for the year ended 31 March 2026 and an operating loss of ¥122 million, an improvement from the prior year's ¥900 million loss but still far from the economics of Electronic Materials. [Composite Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/compositematerials/index.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

In the portfolio context, this division still mattered: it kept Nittobo exposed to a wider industrial cycle and preserved manufacturing scale in glass fiber beyond the narrow Special Glass niche. But it did not drive the equity story.

## Materials Solution: Where the Textile Legacy Now Sat

Materials Solution was the cleanest correction to the legacy dossier narrative. Nittobo's own business page said this division operated the glass fiber for industrial materials, chemical, and textiles businesses. In other words, the original textile inheritance still existed, but it had been folded into a broader solution-oriented bucket alongside industrial glass-fiber products and specialty chemicals. The division generated ¥9.515 billion of sales and ¥588 million of operating profit in the year ended 31 March 2026. [Materials Solution Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/materialssolution/index.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

The page also showed why management kept it: the division covered a wide set of low-profile but real markets, from construction reinforcements and damping materials to functional polymers, adhesive interlinings and the Nittobo Dishcloth. It was not the growth engine, but it remained a diversified base with optionality for cross-business product development. [Materials Solution Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/materialssolution/index.htm), [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm)

## Insulation Materials: Stable, Cyclical, Capital-Light

The Insulation Materials Business was centered on glass wool, which the company described as a nonflammable, sound-absorbing and heat-insulating material used in houses, buildings, vessels and vehicles through group company Paramount Glass Manufacturing. The division produced ¥15.136 billion of sales and ¥202 million of operating profit in the year ended 31 March 2026. [Insulation Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/insulationmaterials/index.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

Compared with Electronic Materials, the economics were modest. But the business gave Nittobo exposure to building-efficiency regulation and energy-saving themes, as well as a steadier domestic materials market less dependent on the AI-server build cycle. [Insulation Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/insulationmaterials/index.htm)

## One Engine, Several Ballast Tanks

The corrected portfolio picture was therefore not one glass business and three unrelated leftovers but one earnings engine backed by several stabilisers. Electronic Materials carried the valuation narrative. Medical provided a profitable second pillar. Composite Materials, Materials Solution and Insulation Materials supplied industrial breadth, legacy continuity and some earnings ballast.

The FY2026 presentation also showed how management expected that internal hierarchy to persist into the next year rather than reverse. Electronic Materials was guided to rise from ¥61.4 billion to ¥77.0 billion of sales on the company's presentation basis and from ¥19.4 billion to ¥26.0 billion of operating profit, while Medical was guided to edge up from ¥13.9 billion to ¥15.0 billion of sales and from ¥2.4 billion to ¥2.5 billion of operating profit. The other divisions remained important, but their own outlook language was about foundation-building, new products, cost absorption and selective demand recovery, not about becoming the new center of earnings gravity. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

The plan documents reinforced that hierarchy in strategic rather than purely numerical terms. Electronic Materials was tasked with further investment in Special Glass and development of NEZ, V and DXII. Medical was told to expand globally and accelerate product development. Composite Materials was framed around productivity and environmentally friendly processes. Materials Solution was explicitly about creating new businesses across industrial glass fiber, chemicals and textiles, while Insulation Materials was tied to higher-performance products for a stricter building-efficiency regime. [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm), [Medical Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/medical/index.htm), [Composite Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/compositematerials/index.htm), [Materials Solution Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/materialssolution/index.htm), [Insulation Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/insulationmaterials/index.htm)

That was also why management's May 2026 plan revision mattered so much. The company did not pretend the other divisions had disappeared; it simply made clear, through its numbers and organisational chart, that Special Glass had become the centre of gravity around which the rest of the group was now arranged. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf), [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm)

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, glass fiber margin, capex for low-Dk scaling
chapters.body:
## The Numbers Behind the Inflection

The first correction required by the primary filings was one of calendar, not arithmetic. The results released on 12 May 2026 were titled Financial Results for FY2025, but they covered the fiscal year ended 31 March 2026. Several headline figures in secondary summaries were therefore attached to the wrong reporting year even when the numbers themselves were right. In that filing, Nittobo reported ¥118.229 billion of net sales, ¥20.819 billion of operating profit, ¥21.544 billion of ordinary profit and ¥41.770 billion of profit attributable to owners of parent. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

The P&L also showed how sharply operating leverage had swung. Net sales rose 8.4 per cent year on year, but operating profit rose 26.6 per cent and the operating margin expanded to 17.6 per cent from 15.1 per cent. Net profit surged 225.4 per cent, a figure the company said reflected extraordinary income from gain on sale of non-current assets recorded in the third quarter. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

## Revenue Trajectory: From Pre-Inflection Base to AI-Era Mix Shift

Nittobo's integrated-report data gave a clean long arc. Consolidated net sales were ¥85.722 billion in the year ended 31 March 2021, ¥109.035 billion in the year ended 31 March 2025, and ¥118.229 billion in the year ended 31 March 2026. The headline CAGR was respectable rather than explosive; the economic transformation came from mix. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

That mix shift was plain in the margin line. The company moved from an operating margin of 15.1 per cent in the year ended March 2025 to 17.6 per cent in the year ended March 2026 because Special Glass volumes and product mix outpaced the rest of the portfolio. In the full-year presentation, management explicitly tied the profit bridge to strong sales of Special Glass, while also noting higher personnel and depreciation expense as capacity was expanded. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

## Electronic Materials: The Margin Engine in Statutory Form

The statutory segment note showed Electronic Materials generating ¥49.265 billion of net sales and ¥19.391 billion of operating profit. On those figures, the segment's operating margin was roughly 39 per cent. That made the rest of the group legible by subtraction: Medical was profitable but far smaller, while Composite Materials, Materials Solution and Insulation Materials together offered breadth more than margin. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

There was an important disclosure nuance here. In the briefing presentation Nittobo showed Electronic Materials sales of ¥61.4 billion because the presentation included intersegment sales for that division; the statutory results report did not. The difference did not change the investment conclusion, but it did matter for anyone trying to reconcile segment shares or segment margins precisely. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

Management's own wording on the driver was unambiguous. The full-year results said strong demand related to AI servers, plus sales of Special Glass with low thermal expansion properties for semiconductor package substrates and low-dielectric Special Glass, drove the segment's revenue. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

## Balance Sheet and Cash Flow: Stronger Than the Income Statement Alone Suggested

The frozen-window filing also showed a group that had entered the capex phase with a much stronger balance sheet than the older dossier implied. Total assets rose to ¥283.038 billion from ¥223.105 billion, net assets rose to ¥180.383 billion from ¥135.829 billion, and the equity ratio improved to 61.3 per cent from 58.1 per cent. Cash and cash equivalents at period-end reached ¥61.835 billion. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

Operating cash flow was ¥17.296 billion. Investing cash flow was positive ¥22.787 billion because proceeds from sale of non-current assets more than offset capital expenditure, and the company disclosed proceeds of ¥39.053 billion from that asset sale in the cash-flow discussion. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

One of the more telling but underused company metrics was the market-value equity-to-asset ratio, which Nittobo put at 241.0 per cent as of 31 March 2026, up from 67.9 per cent a year earlier. It was a rough internal proxy rather than a canonical valuation multiple, but it captured how decisively the market had rerated the business once Special Glass became identified as an AI infrastructure bottleneck input. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

Shareholder returns were rising at the same time. The full-year results showed total dividends of ¥127.00 per share for the year ended 31 March 2026, up from ¥106.00 a year earlier, and management forecast ¥140.00 for the following year. In other words, the company was not only ploughing more capital into Special Glass; it was also letting the cash-generation improvement reach the distribution line. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

The segment forecast framework showed how management expected the portfolio to behave under that higher-investment regime. On the company's presentation basis, Electronic Materials was expected to add ¥15.6 billion of sales year on year in FY2026, Medical ¥1.2 billion and Composite Materials ¥1.1 billion, while Materials Solution and Insulation were forecast to move only marginally. The financial model therefore remained a thesis about Special Glass scaling first and the rest of the group moving later and more slowly. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

## Capex: From Growth Plan to Accelerated Build-Out

Here again the primary record was more precise than the existing dossier. The original FY2024-2027 medium-term plan had targeted approximately ¥80 billion of four-year capital investment and approximately ¥15 billion of four-year R&D spending. By the May 2026 results briefing, those targets had been revised to approximately ¥120 billion and approximately ¥16 billion respectively, while the FY2027 financial forecast alone contemplated ¥45.0 billion of capital investment, ¥11.6 billion of depreciation and ¥4.6 billion of R&D expense. [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

The most important identified project was the glass cloth expansion in Fukushima. Nittobo's integrated report said that in August 2025 it had decided to expand glass fiber cloth production at the Fukushima Enterprise Center, with production scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of FY2026. METI's formal approval summary was more detailed: it described a Fukushima City project for low-thermal-expansion glass cloth for advanced logic ICs, with supply starting in July 2027, capacity rising by about 200 per cent, required funding of about ¥72 billion and maximum subsidy support of about ¥24 billion. Those figures replaced the smaller and materially wrong numbers that had circulated in secondary coverage. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [METI approval summary](https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/economy/economic_security/semicon/nintei_anpohandoutai_keikaku_27.pdf)

## Guidance, Targets and What the Company Itself Expected Next

Nittobo's own forward numbers were stronger than the original dossier allowed. For the fiscal year ending 31 March 2027, the company forecast ¥137.0 billion of sales, ¥26.0 billion of operating profit, ¥26.0 billion of ordinary profit and ¥17.0 billion of profit attributable to owners of parent. The special point was not just the forecast but the accompanying reset of the medium-term plan: FY2027 targets were raised to ¥155.0 billion of sales, ¥36.0 billion of operating profit and ¥51.0 billion of EBITDA. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

That combination - a 2026 year-end cash build, a 2027 single-year capex plan of ¥45 billion, and a revised four-year capital envelope of roughly ¥120 billion - showed a company that had moved from testing the demand signal to financing against it. The key question after the frozen date was therefore no longer whether AI-linked Special Glass demand existed. It was whether Nittobo could translate that demand into enough qualified capacity without blunting the economics that had made the niche so attractive in the first place.

chapters.title: Multi-year trajectory through low-Dk inflection
chapters.body:
## Earnings Trajectory Through the AI Inflection

Nittobo's disclosure rhythm made the inflection visible in stages, and the dates mattered. The company told the market on 1 August 2025, 6 November 2025, 5 February 2026 and 12 May 2026 - its first-quarter, half-year, third-quarter and full-year release dates for the fiscal year ended 31 March 2026 - that Special Glass demand remained the central earnings driver. [IR Calendar](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/calender.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

## Segment Weight Shift

By the full-year filing, the shift was no longer subtle. Electronic Materials delivered ¥49.265 billion of sales and ¥19.391 billion of operating profit, while consolidated operating profit totaled ¥20.819 billion. In other words, almost the entire margin story sat in the Special Glass franchise, with the other divisions acting as ballast more than as co-equal profit engines. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

The quarterly cadence also showed that the year strengthened as it progressed rather than fading. In the full-year presentation, first-half sales were ¥57.4 billion and second-half sales ¥60.8 billion; first-half operating profit was ¥9.5 billion and second-half operating profit ¥11.4 billion. EBITDA rose to ¥30.1 billion for the full year, with EBITDA margin reaching 25.5 per cent. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

The explanatory language was also consistent across the year. The first page of the May 2026 presentation said that, against a background of robust demand for Special Glass, the electronic materials business had recorded higher revenue and profit year on year, and then paired that backward-looking claim with a FY2027 forecast premised on actively increasing capacity for Special Glass because demand was expected to remain robust. In other words, management used the same causal story for the trailing numbers and the forward guide: strong AI- and communications-linked demand, higher-value mix, and capacity expansion needed to keep up. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

## Capital Expenditure as the Forward Signal

The best forward indicator in Nittobo's own materials was not rhetoric but capital allocation. The 2024 medium-term plan had already promised approximately ¥80 billion of four-year capital investment. By 12 May 2026 management had raised that cumulative figure to approximately ¥120 billion and was guiding to ¥45 billion of capex in the year ending 31 March 2027, alongside a specific August 2025 decision to expand glass-fiber-cloth capacity at Fukushima. [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

## Revisions, Not Just Results

The most revealing disclosure in the frozen window was that management did not merely post a strong year; it revised the outer plan. FY2027 targets were lifted to ¥155 billion of sales and ¥36 billion of operating profit, against the original ¥135 billion and ¥20 billion. That was a stronger signal than a one-quarter guidance tweak. It implied the board had concluded the AI-led Special Glass demand curve was not a short-lived inventory event but a structural opportunity worth financing against. [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

The dividend line carried the same message. Nittobo proposed a year-end dividend of ¥99.50 per share for FY2025 in company nomenclature, taking the full-year total to ¥127.00, and said it planned ¥140.00 for the following year. A company that feared a near-term collapse in the Special Glass cycle would not normally have paired such a large capex plan with an upgraded outer plan and a higher dividend schedule. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

Management's own narrative around the year also grew more confident. In the integrated report, the company said the market demand it was seeing had increased by about two to three times versus the assumptions embedded when the medium-term plan was formulated. That observation sat awkwardly with any attempt to describe 2025-2026 as just another ordinary electronics upcycle. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

Yet the issuer never presented the cycle as risk-free. In the same May 2026 materials it said the FY2027 environment remained uncertain because of Middle East tensions, logistics costs, material-procurement risk, exchange-rate volatility and continued weakness in China. The earnings story that emerged from the primary record was therefore more nuanced than a simple boom narrative: volumes, mix and margins were all rising, but management was funding that rise while explicitly acknowledging a more unstable macro and geopolitical backdrop. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

The medium-term plan supplied the policy frame around that cadence. It said the group would keep a basic shareholder-return policy of at least ¥55 per share and a payout ratio targeting 30 per cent of steady earnings, while also using performance above operating-profit thresholds to fund additional employee bonuses. Read alongside the 2025-2026 earnings trajectory, that policy suggested management viewed the Special Glass windfall not as a one-off to be hoarded, but as a stronger earnings base on which both reinvestment and stakeholder payouts could be layered. [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

## Structural Risks Embedded in the Cycle

The company itself did not treat the boom as risk-free. In the full-year report and risk disclosures it flagged higher energy costs, raw-material procurement risk, exchange-rate volatility, demand swings in IT-related printed circuit boards and semiconductor package substrates, and the possibility that capital investments could under-earn if demand forecasts changed materially. The earnings story, then, was not one of a frictionless secular compounder. It was one of a specialty materials maker using unusually strong margins to fund a very large and very time-sensitive supply response. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [Business risks](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/risk.htm)

chapters.title: Representative Director, executive team, board governance
chapters.body:
## A Different Name at the Top by the Frozen Date

By 1 April 2026 Nittobo's leadership page had changed at the top. Hisanobu Hayashi was listed as Representative and Chief Executive Officer; Hiroyuki Tada, who had become Representative and Chief Executive Officer in April 2024, was listed as Director and Deputy Chairman. That transition mattered because it marked the move from the initial FY2024-2027 plan launch under Tada to the next execution phase under Hayashi. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html)

## Hiroyuki Tada and the First Phase of the Plan

The dated corporate record on the directors-and-officers page showed Tada joining the company in 1985, moving through the textile and glass-fiber businesses, becoming Representative and Chief Executive Officer in April 2024, and shifting to Deputy Chairman in April 2026. Over that interval the group's reported operating profit rose to ¥20.819 billion in the year ended 31 March 2026, effectively clearing the original FY2027 medium-term target of ¥20 billion one year early. The May 2026 briefing then raised the FY2027 target to ¥36 billion and the four-year capital-investment envelope to roughly ¥120 billion. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html), [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

## The 1 April 2026 Executive Line-Up

Nittobo's current executive table showed a management team arranged plainly around the business portfolio. Hayashi served as CEO. Yasushi Okahisa was Representative Managing Executive Officer and Division General Manager of the Corporate Management Division. Akimasa Kajita ran the Electronic Materials Business Division. Masao Fukushima ran Medical, Masaki Ito Composite Materials, Shotaro Yasuda Materials Solution, and Yuichi Ameda Insulation Materials. The company disclosed 15 executive officers in total as of 1 April 2026. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html), [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

That line-up was itself revealing. By the frozen date the specialty glass business was not a side franchise inside an old textile group; it was one of the principal operating seats around which the current executive bench had been structured. The Electronic Materials division even had multiple deputy division general managers in the published officer table - Takehiro Mikami, Hirokazu Nagata and So Shigeoka - signalling where managerial density had accumulated. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html)

The full officer table filled out the rest of the management bench. Katsuya Hatanaka served as deputy general manager of Medical; Koichi Nakamura led the Technology Development Division; Hiroyuki Tanida was deputy general manager of Composite Materials; and Haruka Yamazaki oversaw Risk Management and the Legal Department within the Corporate Management Division. The structure showed that the company was not simply elevating a single glass-fiber executive; it was publishing a cross-divisional command map in which technology, risk, legal and corporate-finance functions had clearly identified owners alongside the business-division heads. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html)

## Board Architecture

The governance report said Nittobo had operated as a company with Nomination Committee, etc. since shareholder approval in June 2014. As of 1 April 2026, the board had seven directors, including four external directors, and the company disclosed that its articles capped the board at 12 members. Each statutory committee - Nomination, Remuneration and Audit - had five members and was chaired by an external director. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf), [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html)

The current directors page named the three internal directors as Yuichi Tsuji, Hiroyuki Tada and Takanobu Matsunaga, and the four external directors as Sadayoshi Fujishige, Agasa Naito, Yasuharu Nakajima and Takeshi Miida. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html)

The governance report gave those outside directors more institutional texture than the older dossier had. Fujishige was described as a former top manager of listed companies and chaired the Nomination Committee. Agasa Naito was described as a legal expert and outside officer at other companies. Nakajima, a certified public accountant, chaired the Audit Committee. Miida brought listed-company manufacturing experience and chaired the Remuneration Committee. All four were designated independent. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The same report also showed how Nittobo had tried to align itself with the post-2015 Japanese governance template. It said the company complied with all principles of the revised June 2021 Corporate Governance Code, delegated as much operating authority as legally possible to executive officers, and maintained a board with outside directors at least equal in number to internal directors. The skill areas the board said it wanted represented included corporate management, technology and R&D, sales and marketing, global business, finance and accounting, legal affairs and risk management, and HR and personnel development. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The governance report also described a live evaluation process rather than a symbolic one. It said the board carried out annual effectiveness evaluations using questionnaires, with external attorneys involved to enhance independence and objectivity in supervising the content and analyzing the results. The Audit Committee, meanwhile, was described as meeting at least once a month, a detail that mattered given how much of the group's current execution risk sat in capex oversight, quality control and legal exposure. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

## Ownership and Pay Discipline

The April 2026 governance report put foreign shareholding in the 10 per cent to less than 20 per cent range. The March 31, 2026 stock-information page identified The Master Trust Bank of Japan (trust account) as the largest shareholder with 3.331 million shares, or 9.11 per cent of shares excluding treasury stock; Nippon Life Insurance held 4.41 per cent, and Custody Bank of Japan (trust account) 3.83 per cent. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf), [Stock information](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/memo.htm)

The same stock page filled in the next layer of ownership that earlier summaries had misstated. Dai-ichi Life held 3.60 per cent, Custody Bank of Japan's taxable trust account 3.26 per cent, and Sumitomo Realty & Development 3.26 per cent. The governance report separately said the company sold six cross-shareholding positions for ¥1,957 million in fiscal 2024, a small but concrete sign that the board was willing to reduce older relationship holdings rather than defend them reflexively. [Stock information](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/memo.htm), [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The human-capital disclosures, while not central to the Special Glass thesis, added to the governance picture. The April 2026 report said Nittobo was targeting 10 per cent female representation in management positions by fiscal 2030, reported the fiscal 2024 result at 8.3 per cent, and said male childcare-leave take-up had reached 61.5 per cent. These figures did not change the earnings model, but they showed the company was publishing measurable internal-governance and workforce targets rather than speaking only in abstract principles. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The same governance report also showed a pay system more formulaic than the older dossier suggested. For the representative-executive tier, remuneration was structured as 60 per cent basic pay, 25 per cent company-performance-linked cash and 15 per cent stock remuneration when the performance-linked component was at 100 per cent. The stock plan granted 2,360 base points to the Representative and Chief Executive Officer, with one point convertible into one share at vesting, and capped the performance-linked coefficient at 1.5. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The formula was spelled out in some detail. Company-performance-linked cash was based on operating profit and ROE, while individual-performance-linked cash depended on divisional operating profit versus budget and on personal evaluation. For fiscal 2024 metrics used in fiscal 2025 remuneration, the company disclosed actual operating profit of ¥16.4 billion against a medium-term-plan target of ¥12.5 billion, which is why the incentive structure had already begun paying on a much stronger curve before Hayashi took over. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The report also laid out the ladder below the CEO tier. Base stock-remuneration points were 1,219 for senior managing executive officers, 903 for managing executive officers, 452 for senior executive officers and 409 for executive officers, with the performance-linked coefficient determined by actual operating profit relative to the medium-term-plan target and capped at 1.5. That level of formulaic disclosure made it easier to see how management was being paid to execute a multiyear Special Glass expansion rather than to maximize a single year's accounting profit. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The governance architecture also clarified who did not control the company. Nittobo disclosed that it had no parent company and no controlling shareholder. That left a structure more typical of a Japanese listed industrial with a mixed domestic institutional register, some cross-shareholdings still in place, foreign ownership in the low-teens range, and a majority-independent board. It did not remove governance risk, but it did mean the Special Glass investment program was being overseen without an obvious parent-level capital-allocation veto. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf), [Stock information](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/memo.htm)

Nittobo's governance was therefore not especially dramatic by post-reform Japanese standards. What mattered was that by the frozen date the board and executive structure had already been reshaped around a much larger Special Glass opportunity, and the compensation and ownership disclosures showed management being measured against that capital-intensive bet rather than against preservation of a legacy conglomerate status quo.

The administrative calendar underscored how close this transition sat to the frozen date. The full-year results filing set June 18, 2026 as the scheduled annual-securities-report filing date and June 19, 2026 as the scheduled ordinary general meeting date, with dividend payment from June 22. The dossier therefore captured Nittobo in a narrow interregnum: Hayashi was already CEO, Tada had already moved upstairs, and the market had already seen the plan revision, but the formal annual meeting that would ratify the next stage still sat just beyond the freeze. [FY2026 financial results](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/202884/00.pdf)

That timing mattered because it framed Hayashi's inheritance precisely. He took charge only after the company had already locked in a much larger capital plan, a much stronger dividend trajectory and a very public commitment to faster Special Glass scaling. The leadership question in the dossier was therefore less about whether he would initiate the pivot than about whether he and the operating bench published on April 1, 2026 could industrialise it without weakening the product-quality lead on which the margin structure depended. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html), [FY2026 results presentation](https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/3110/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym3/202886/00.pdf)

The committee architecture further reinforced how formalised that oversight had become. Each of the three statutory committees had five members, with one internal and four external directors, and all three were chaired by outside directors. In practice that meant nominations, pay and audit were all structured so that the internal executives driving the Special Glass expansion did not dominate the committee process by sheer numbers. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

The governance report also linked that formal structure to shareholder dialogue. It said the company published disclosures required under Japanese and foreign rules, described timely and appropriate IR activity as part of its effort to improve corporate value, and framed board supervision around medium- to long-term corporate-value growth rather than around a narrow quarterly lens. For a company whose central question had become how hard to press a technically constrained growth lane, that longer-horizon framing was not incidental; it was the governance context in which the Special Glass investment program was being justified. [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf), [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm)

That was why the top-table change mattered more than the formal title swap alone. Tada had presided over the phase in which the market finally understood Nittobo's Special Glass economics; Hayashi inherited the harder phase in which those economics had to be converted into durable industrial scale. The governance materials did not resolve whether that transition would succeed, but they did make plain that the company knew it was moving from a planning-and-rerating story into an execution-and-capacity story. [Directors and officers](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/sustainability/governance/executive.html), [Corporate Governance Report](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/nittobo_CG_20260401-EN.pdf)

chapters.title: PCB substrate manufacturers, AI server supply chain, manufacturing footprint
chapters.body:
## Glass Fiber at the Base of the Stack

Nittobo's own public materials described the business in application terms rather than by brand-name customer list. The Electronic Materials page said the company supplied Special Glass for printed wiring-board materials supporting high-speed communications and semiconductor innovation. The 2025 integrated report then mapped those applications more concretely: low-dielectric motherboards for AI servers and network switches, and low-CTE semiconductor package substrates for CPUs, GPUs, ASICs, DRAM and NAND. [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

That application-based disclosure was the important correction to the earlier dossier. In the filings and company pages reviewed through 23 May 2026, Nittobo did not publish a verified list of laminate-company customers by name. What it did publish was the layer of the stack in which it participated and the materials functions it provided.

## What the Company Actually Disclosed About the Chain

| Nittobo material | Disclosed application | Function in the stack |
|---|---|---|
| NE-glass | Motherboards for AI servers and network switches | Low dielectric constant and low dissipation factor for higher-speed transmission |
| NER-glass | Higher-speed communications equipment beyond NE-glass use cases | Lower-loss extension of the low-Dk platform |
| T-glass | Semiconductor package substrates for CPUs, GPUs, ASICs and other advanced packages | Low thermal expansion and high tensile elasticity to limit warping |
| Ultra-thin glass cloth and other Special Glass variants | Printed wiring boards and advanced electronic materials | Thickness, signal and processing performance improvements |

These were not generic materials claims. On the current product pages, NE-glass was disclosed with a 1 GHz dielectric constant of 4.8 and a dielectric dissipation factor of 0.0015, against 6.8 and 0.0035 for E-glass. T-glass was disclosed with a thermal expansion coefficient of 2.8 x10^-6/°C, against 5.6 for E-glass. [NE-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/ne-glass.htm), [T-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/t-glass.htm), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

## Manufacturing Footprint and Supply Position

The business-locations page showed the Japanese manufacturing and development footprint more clearly than the older write-up did. Nittobo listed the Fukushima Enterprise Center, including the former Fukushima No.1 and No.2 factories, and the Fukuyama Enterprise Center in Koriyama, where the page also located the Technology Development Division. The centennial history page separately recorded the build-out in Taiwan: the 1988 establishment of the predecessor to NITTOBO ASIA Glass Fiber, the 2019 consolidation of Baotek Industrial Materials, and the 2021 establishment of a new Special Glass factory at NAG. [Business locations](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/corporate/location/index.htm), [Nittobo History](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/100th_anv/eng/history.html)

At the group level, the risk disclosures said Nittobo conducted production activities in Japan, Taiwan, the U.S. and China and sold products globally. That mattered because it anchored the supply chain in a real operating footprint rather than in a single prefecture factory myth. [Business risks](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/risk.htm)

## Where the AI Demand Entered

The integrated report was explicit that the AI demand signal reached Nittobo through communications and packaging, not through direct server assembly. In the logic segment it said Special Glass was being used in low-dielectric motherboards for AI servers and network switches and in low-CTE packages for CPUs, GPUs and ASICs. In the memory segment it said the material was being used in low-dielectric packages for DRAM and had started expanding into low-CTE packages for NAND memory. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

That description placed Nittobo upstream of the laminator, substrate and board-manufacturing layers even when the company declined to name each customer. The chain was therefore visible enough to understand technologically, if not granular enough to assign every revenue yen to a named laminate buyer.

## A Supply Chain That Stayed Application-Led in Public

Nittobo's public disclosures were unusually strong on physics and unusually reserved on customer names. They made clear what the materials did, where in the motherboard and package stack they sat, and where the group manufactured them. They did not, through the frozen date, provide a company-verified roll call of laminate or PCB buyers.

That left the correct research conclusion narrower but more reliable than the older dossier's named-customer table: Nittobo was an upstream Special Glass supplier into the high-speed communications and semiconductor package-substrate chain, with disclosed production and development nodes in Fukushima, Koriyama and Taiwan, and with AI-server demand arriving through printed wiring boards, switches, routers and advanced packaging rather than through direct sales to hyperscalers. [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [Business locations](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/corporate/location/index.htm)

The October 2025 TPCA Show release added one more useful clue to how the supply chain was being cultivated in practice. Nittobo Taiwan said it would exhibit low-CTE glass, low-DK glass and ultra-thin glass cloth at one of the PCB industry's main Taiwan trade shows, making the company's customer-development effort in the island's circuit-board ecosystem an official matter of record rather than an inference from geography alone. [TPCA Show Taipei 2025 release](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/news/pdf/20251008_newsrelease.pdf)

chapters.title: Where Nitto Boseki sits against Asahi Kasei/AGY, Taiwan Glass, Owens Corning, China Jushi
chapters.body:
## Competition Measured in Material Properties, Not Brand Lists

The most reliable primary-source way to understand Nittobo's competitive position is to begin with the property gap it disclosed between Special Glass and ordinary E-glass. On the NE-glass page, the company gave a 1 GHz dielectric constant of 4.8 versus 6.8 for E-glass and a dielectric dissipation factor of 0.0015 versus 0.0035. On the T-glass page, it gave a thermal expansion coefficient of 2.8 x10^-6/°C versus 5.6 for E-glass, along with higher tensile strength and modulus. Those were the performance deltas that made the niche valuable. [NE-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/ne-glass.htm), [T-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/t-glass.htm)

## What Management Itself Said About Rivalry

Nittobo's 2025 integrated report was more candid than the older dossier acknowledged. Management said Chinese and Taiwanese companies were aggressively catching up in the Special Glass sector, which ruled out any complacent claim that the field had remained frozen. Yet the same passage said the company retained an overwhelming competitive advantage in both quality and production capacity for low-thermal-expansion glass and intended to maintain it. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

The company's public risk disclosures used even broader language. They warned that intensified competition from domestic and foreign competitors, the development of alternative materials for glass fiber, or delays in new-technology development could materially affect results and financial condition. That was the official competitive framing: a premium technical niche with genuine barriers, but not one insulated from foreign catch-up or substitution risk. [Business risks](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/risk.htm)

## The Moat the Company Actually Claimed

Three elements of moat were explicitly or implicitly documented in primary sources. First was composition and property performance: T-glass and NE-glass were not marketing labels for commodity E-glass, but different formulations with disclosed mechanical, thermal and dielectric advantages. [T-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/t-glass.htm), [NE-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/ne-glass.htm)

Second was manufacturing capability. The integrated report and the August 2025 METI approval both pointed to low-thermal-expansion glass cloth as a capacity-constrained strategic product requiring large, specific investment in Fukushima. The same primary materials repeatedly described Nittobo as an integrated producer with spinning and weaving capability, and the company tied that integration directly to its competitive position. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [METI approval summary](https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/economy/economic_security/semicon/nintei_anpohandoutai_keikaku_27.pdf)

Third was roadmap control. The medium-term plan said Nittobo would develop next-generation Special Glass - NEZ, V and DXII - and proceed to mass production after identifying customer needs. The integrated report's technical roadmap separately identified Vlex as the low-CTE, low-loss performance target beyond today's T-glass. That mattered because it showed the company competing on successive materials generations, not just harvesting an installed-base advantage. [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

The roadmap disclosed in the integrated report made the competitive logic more concrete. Nittobo mapped NE, NER and NEZ against successively faster wired-telecom and switch applications, from 100 GbE and 400 GbE through 800 GbE and higher-bandwidth AI front-end and back-end networks. It mapped T and Vlex against low-CTE substrate needs as packages and system interconnect speeds climbed. That did not prove permanent dominance, but it did show the company competing on a moving technical frontier rather than on a static installed product. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

The October 2025 TPCA show release gave a second official glimpse of how Nittobo intended to defend that position commercially. Rather than exhibiting only current products, the company said it would showcase next-generation Special Glass - low-CTE glass, low-DK glass and ultra-thin glass cloth - at a PCB-focused exhibition in Taipei. That suggested a company trying to widen specification control and customer familiarity before competitors could compress the window. [TPCA Show Taipei 2025 release](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/news/pdf/20251008_newsrelease.pdf)

The company's broader business pages supported that reading. Electronic Materials was described not just as a seller of raw glass but as an integrated developer of glass compositions and products, while the integrated report repeatedly stressed the value of having both spinning and weaving capabilities in-house. In a niche where low-CTE and low-loss performance had to survive conversion from chemistry to yarn to cloth to laminate, that integration was one of the few moats the company itself was willing to emphasize repeatedly in public. [Electronic Materials Business](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/index.htm), [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf)

The published property tables also showed why the competition could not be reduced to a single number. In the integrated report's comparison matrix, T-glass, NE-glass and NER-glass were differentiated not just by dielectric constant but by thermal expansion, tensile elasticity and target application, from AI-server motherboards and switch boards to package substrates. That mattered because a rival did not merely need a low-DK yarn or a low-CTE cloth in isolation; it needed the right combination of properties in the right form factor at production scale. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [T-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/t-glass.htm), [NE-glass](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/business/electronicmaterials/ne-glass.htm)

## The Corrected Competitive Picture

The older dossier's named-peer lists were less defensible than Nittobo's own disclosures. Through the frozen date, the company itself did not provide a verified, exhaustive list of peer producers with market-share splits. What it did provide was enough to support a firmer, narrower conclusion: the competition was between commodity E-glass and a smaller Special Glass field; Chinese and Taiwanese companies were catching up; Nittobo believed it still held the lead in low-thermal-expansion glass quality and capacity; and the next competitive battleground had already moved to NEZ, V, DXII and Vlex. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [Business risks](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/risk.htm), [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm)

That left Nittobo in a strong but not static position. It was not the simple caricature of a monopoly supplier immune to imitation. It was a technically advanced incumbent whose moat still rested on property performance, qualified manufacturing capacity and product-generation cadence - and whose own disclosures showed that management understood the catch-up risk well before the market narrative began to flatten it.

The most defensible competitive conclusion inside the frozen window was therefore slightly narrower than the popular one but arguably more useful. Nittobo looked less like an undisputed sole source across all advanced PCB glass and more like the quality-and-capacity leader in the low-thermal-expansion and low-loss corner of the market, one whose advantage was real enough for management to say so, but fragile enough that the company kept spelling out the next product generation and the next production build-out in the same breath. [Integrated Report 2025](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/pdf/Nittobo_Integrated-Report_2025.pdf), [Medium-Term Management Plan](https://www.nittobo.co.jp/eng/ir/keiei/chukei.htm)
